02.text: Cottontail bounced in, all spots and hurry.
"Come on, come ON! Come meet my dirt friend!"

Down in the garden, a garden bed rumpled.
It heaved. It sat up. And it whistled hello —
a jaguar! Brown as the brownest of earth,
with a leaf-green tuft and a wide slow smile
and soil in his whiskers and worms for neighbors.
whistled Dirt, in a voice deep as wells.
"You woke me. That's fine. I was nearly done anyway."

03.text:
Dirt gave a tour at the speed of a garden,
which is slow.
"Here's my beans. Here's my roots. Here's my dark."
He held up a seed, very small, very brown.

"It sleeps in the ground, where it's boring on purpose.
That's how it grows. Sleep first. Then flowers."
Winds yawned. (It was catching.) Moon poked at a worm.
"You just can't see it. That's the best part."

Nobody quite agreed.
Dirt didn't mind. Dirt never minds.
Gardens are used to being underestimated.

04.text:
Meanwhile, below the castle — below the below,
where the cellars stop pretending to be rooms —
three shadows were meeting a stranger.

Blue. All-over blue. Blue face, blue fingers,
blue as the hour before the morning.
she said, like they'd talked just yesterday.

"I'm Blooey. The fifth one. The last one.
There were five little beds in the tower, remember?
You kept mine made. That was kind."

Evilest stared. Beedlist held her book tighter.
Even Shock, who is taller than secrets, went still.
And in the blue hands sat a little clay pot,
small as a teacup,
and empty,
and patient.

05.text:
"We fought them. Fighting wakes people up.
So we won't lift a finger. We'll just be around:
a creak at nap time. A drip in the quiet.
A little too much of the wrong kind of nothing.

Tired people leak. Upset people spill.
And my little pot catches spills."
She turned the pot slowly around in her hands.

"Drip by drip, sisters. Nobody will notice.
Nobody guards against nothing at all."

06.text:
Nap time at the castle. Curtains drawn. Cozy.
Then: tap. Then: creeeeak. Then a moth at the window.
Then somebody's spoon, somewhere, stirring forever.

Moon flipped and she flopped and she flumped and she huffed —
and a tiny gold spark hopped right off of her huff,
and rolled down the stair, and the wall, and the dark,
and dripped in a pot she had never once seen.

Plip.
Far below, a small blue smile.
… But the growing happens while you sleep.

07.text:
Now here is a thing that had never, not once,
not ever in five whole books, happened before:
"You're on my side of the sleep,"

her sister snapped back.

The room went so quiet the curtains looked shocked.
The twins who agree — who were born agreeing —
lay glaring, too tired to remember they matched.

And down in the dark the pot glowed brighter,
gold sloshing inside like a small stolen sunset.
Blooey didn't gloat. Well. Mostly.

08.text:
Cottontail knew what to do about villains.
Claws. It was claws. It had always been claws.
She prowled every hallway. She pounced on a creak.
The creak was a floorboard. You can't arrest those.

Winds threw the whole sky at the problem, gladly:
he blew the moth west and the tapping to sea.
But you can't blow away an already-lost nap.
It's already lost. The tired stays tired.

growled Cottontail, claws full of nothing.
And nothing, politely, was all that she got.

09.text:
By the third bad morning, the shine had gone somewhere.
Moon's wings went up — and the rest of Moon didn't.
Baby Lady said

and it came out a whisper,
so small that the fish all leaned out of the sea to hear.

Purple Shine tried mama-magic. Pink Shine tried papa's:
warm blankets, warm soup, the lullaby twice.
But you can't pour sleep into somebody spilling.

said Moon, very quietly.
And that, right there, was the whole of the trouble. … But the growing happens while you sleep.

10.text:
That evening there came a knock — soft, unhurried —
and there on the doorstep stood somebody blue,
with a pot full of nearly-all-of-the-gold.

"You dropped it. I caught it. There's just a bit left.
One more bad bedtime should do it."

Then feet on the stairs — it was Cheeblest, breathless,
bows flying loose like they do when it matters:

"It's her! The fifth bed! It's HER!
Don't be upset — DON'T BE UPSET — it feeds the—"

11.text:
And into that worried and wobbling room
came a whistle. Low. Slow. Deep as wells.

Dirt stood in the doorway with soil on his paws,
not one bit surprised and not one bit hurried.

"Can't out-shout it.
But I know the thing. I do it all seasons.
Come and lie down in my garden."
said Dirt, with his wide slow smile.

12.text:
So out they went, under the round yellow moon,
and lay themselves down in the warm brown earth —
a moon-girl, a puppy, a mama, a papa,
two jaguar cubs — in rows, like the beans.

And Dirt went along the row, tucking:
a pat of warm soil for a blanket's corner,
a leaf pulled up here, a worm shooed off there.
he whistled, low as a root.

And the castle hushed, and the garden held them,
and one by one by two by three,
the whole tired family
slept. … But the growing happens while you sleep.

15.text:
Blooey sat down in the bits of her pot,
and for somebody blue, she looked awfully grey.

"And I kept all the watch.
Somebody had to stay up, keeping count.
Nobody let me — nobody ever —"

She stopped.
She was tired. It's hard to say tired things.

And Cheeblest — who once had been forgiven herself,
back when forgiving was newly invented —
came and patted the warm brown earth beside her.

"That's how it starts.
You get to be a seed too."
